newsitem.title: CHINA: China's regulators to meet firms for listing.
newsitem.headline: China's regulators to meet firms for listing.

text.p: China's securities regulators will meet this week with officials of the 38 companies cleared for foreign share offers to ensure they are aware of the obligations under public offerings, officials said on Monday.

Discussions at the meeting to be held in Nanjing in eastern China would cover requirements for the public disclosure of information as well as corporate financial reports and auditing, officials of the China Securities Regulatory Commission told Reuters.
Chinese companies listed outside the country have generally been better at meeting these requirements than those firms listed only on domestic stock markets.

Several companies have run into difficulties with Hong Kong regulators for lack of disclosure of information as well as failing to use funds raised from public offers for the purpose stated in their prospectus.

Most of the Chinese companies that have listed their shares outside the country have done so in Hong Kong. The latest batch, given approval by market regulators last month, will likely focus their share offers on the Hong Kong market, securities industry executives say.
